newsitem.title: UK: HSBC shares set record high.
newsitem.headline: HSBC shares set record high.

text.p: Shares in HSBC Holdings Plc reached a record high on Thursday amid a series of positive influences ranging from recent strength in bond markets to vague rumours of a link with a German bank, traders and analysts said.

HSBC is also said to have recently held meetings with fund managers following buoyant first-half results last month. And an agreement between the UK and China on a new container terminal, after the Hong Kong market closed, also boosted sentiment.
The stock was up 23-1/2p at 12.08-1/2 stg by 1436 GMT, after earlier rising as high as 12.12 stg -- surpassing its previous intraday peak of 12.09 stg set on September 17.
Trading volume reached a moderate 2.4 million shares.

Traders and analysts played down talk of a link with a German bank but said HSBC was expected to make further expansion moves. "They will take out other banks but just who we don't know," said one head of equity sales.
Another added, "They are not in any great rush to spend their money and the main thrust is to build their position in Asia outside Hong Kong.
"They have the capability if something comes up in Europe to move opportunistically, but I don't think it is their priority."
